extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs’ multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.publisher: University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involves an automated coarse filtering of samples from six existing benchmarks using LLM inspectors to ensure visual dependency and minimal data leakage, followed by a strict manual review by three experts to curate 1,500 high-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples from six existing multi-modal benchmarks, including two focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Samples were first coarsely filtered using LLMs, after which three experts conducted a manual review to select samples based on visual dependency, coverage of capability dimensions, and the requirement of advanced multi-modal abilities.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs (including GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B) were used for coarse filtering to check visual dependency and leakage, and 16 LVLMs (including GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series) were used to gauge sample difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently faces the risk of eventual accidental data leakage into model training corpora, as it is not yet a dynamic test set.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed as a benchmark for testing and evaluating the actual multi-modal capabilities of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to update the benchmark by expanding it into a larger, online test set and introducing dynamic evaluation methods to prevent future data leakage.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was manually sampled and balanced to ensure diversity across capability dimensions and difficulty levels, resulting in exactly 250 samples for each of the 6 core capabilities and an even distribution across 18 detailed axes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated filtering pipeline was used to remove samples that did not meet visual dependency and minimal data leakage criteria. Eight LLMs were used as inspectors, and only samples that were answered correctly by two or fewer LLMs were retained.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We first choose two benchmarks [27, 21] focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge [51, 30, 20, 29] for our sample collection.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: After the coarse filtering with LLM inspectors, we further employ three experts to conduct the manual review process to ensure: 1) each sample’s answer should be based on the understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we use eight powerful LLMs as candidates inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage, including two closed-source APIs (GPT4-Turbo [34], and GeminiPro [41]) and six leading open-source models (e.g., LLaMA-70B [43], Qwen-1.5-72B [1], and Mixtral-8x7B [19]). [...] Then we use 16 leading LVLMs (e.g., GPT4V [35], GeminiPro-Vision [41], LLaVA series [24, 26]) to gauge the difficulty of the samples and split them to four levels.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: In the future, we plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM’s and LVLM’s training corpora.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: MMStar benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs’ multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: In the future, we plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM’s and LVLM’s training corpora.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Finally, after considering both the diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels, we manually curated 1,500 high-quality samples from the coarsely filtered set. [...] Each core capability contains a meticulously balanced 250 samples. We further ensure a relatively even distribution across the 18 detailed axes.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We then develop an automated pipeline to preliminarily filter out samples that do not meet the first two criteria. Specifically, we employ two closed-source LLMs [41, 34] and six open-source LLMs [1, 42, 49, 3, 19, 43] sizing 20B or larger to serve as inspectors. [...] Finally, we only retain those samples with hit counts of two or fewer hits, indicating that around 75% of LLM inspectors fail to provide the correct answer.
